cards.front: What changes were made to the elftools submodule in vg v1.76.1?

cards.front: How are gref vcfs compatible with vcfbub in vg v1.76.1?
cards.back: gref vcfs now compatible with vcfbub via fixed LV symantics.

cards.front: What was omitted from VCF headers in vg v1.76.1?
cards.back: Unused contigs omitted from VCF headers.

cards.front: What commands are marked as deprecated in vg v1.77.0?
cards.back: `vg mcmc` and `vg genotype` are marked as deprecated.

cards.front: How does `vg call` behave in vg v1.77.0?
cards.back: `vg call` will call against a non-reference path if you explicitly ask.

cards.front: What error does `vg augment -i` produce in vg v1.77.0?
cards.back: `vg augment -i` errors when it is told to embed a path without a name.

cards.front: What improvements were made to `vg snarls --traversals` in vg v1.77.0?
cards.back: `vg snarls --traversals` related helptext improved and useful errors added.

cards.front: What happened to `vg snarls --pathnames` in vg v1.77.0?
cards.back: `vg snarls --pathnames` option removed (didn't really work).

cards.front: How are snarl ids in vg deconstruct vcfs consistent in vg v1.77.0?
cards.back: Snarl ids in vg deconstruct vcfs now consistent with vg call (forward on reference).

cards.front: What changes were made to the gref segments algorithm in vg v1.77.0?
cards.back:
Make gref segments table more BED-like, and easier to filter by snarl level.
Simplify gref segments algorithm; make it greedier on length and only consider things well-anchored to a reference.

cards.front: What new option was added to `vg deconstruct` and `vg call` in vg v1.77.0?
cards.back: `vg deconstruct -L` option ported to `vg call` to cluster big alleles. Both now support deletions. Remains experimental.

cards.front: What was removed in vg v1.77.0?
cards.back: `vg chain` and associated iterator used only in testing were removed.

cards.front: What changes were made to the manpage generator in vg v1.77.0?
cards.back: Manpage generator is required to include non-deprecated subcommands (and is updated to do so).

cards.front: What new file is included in vg v1.77.0?
cards.back: A `CONTRIBUTING.md` file was added.

cards.front: What was clarified in vg v1.77.0 regarding `vg map --gbwt-name`?
cards.back: `vg map --gbwt-name` option was explained (resolves #1429).

cards.front: What optimizations were made to `vg giraffe` chaining modes in vg v1.77.0?
cards.back: `vg giraffe` chaining mode (`-b hifi`, `-b r10`, `-b chaining-sr`) memory & speed optimizations; no effect on output.

cards.front: What GBZ version support was added in vg v1.77.0?
cards.back: Support for GBZ version 3 (vg still writes version 2 by default).

cards.front: What new option was added to `vg gbwt` in vg v1.77.0?
cards.back: `vg gbwt` option `--gbz-version` for selecting the version of output GBZ.

cards.front: What change was made to `vg construct -S` in vg v1.77.0?
cards.back: `vg construct -S` will automatically turn on `-f` (resolves #2932).

cards.front: How does `vg giraffe --max-chains-per-tree` work in vg v1.77.0?
cards.back: `vg giraffe --max-chains-per-tree` works as documented (bugfix).

cards.front: What change was made to `vg giraffe --min-chains` in vg v1.77.0?
cards.back: `vg giraffe --min-chains` is now `--target-alignment-attempts` and has better documentation.

cards.front: What requirement was added to `vg surject` in vg v1.77.0?
cards.back: `vg surject` now requires either `-i`/`--interleaved` or `-U`/`--force-unpaired` if it thinks the input smells like paired-end data.

cards.front: How does `vg giraffe` now use the GAM fragment length distribution in vg v1.77.0?
cards.back: `vg giraffe` now uses the GAM fragment length distribution built-in field, like `vg map`, instead of a `"fragment_length_distribution"` annotation.

cards.front: How does `dozeu` behave in vg v1.77.0?
cards.back: `dozeu` respects X-drop definition more strictly.

cards.front: What change was made to `vg gamsort` in vg v1.77.0?
cards.back: `vg gamsort` no longer crashes with very large GAM files.

cards.front: How does `vg gamsort` sort GAF in vg v1.77.0?
cards.back: `vg gamsort` sorts GAF by GBWT node id intervals for better compatibility with GAF-base.

cards.front: What new option was added to `vg gamsort` in vg v1.77.0?
cards.back: `vg gamsort` option `--two-merge-rounds` to guarantee at most two rounds of merges when sorting GAF.

cards.front: How does `vg giraffe` and `vg surject` handle paired-end reads in vg v1.77.0?
cards.back: `vg giraffe` and `vg surject` now surject paired-end reads with the same code.

cards.front: What change was made to submodule URLs in vg v1.77.0?
cards.back: `cairo` and `pixman` submodules pulled from `https://gitlab.freedesktop.org` instead of `git://anongit.freedesktop.org` since the latter seems to have broken.

cards.front: How does `vg giraffe` chaining mode handle multiplicities in vg v1.77.0?
cards.back: Avoid underflowing multiplicities in `vg giraffe` chaining mode (caused erroneous MAPQ 0).

cards.front: What is GBZ?
cards.back:
A compressed graph format that combines:
- Graph topology (nodes + edges)
- GBWT (haplotype paths)
- Reference path metadata

The primary graph format for Giraffe.

cards.front: What is GBWT?
cards.back:
Graph Burrows-Wheeler Transform. A compressed representation
of haplotype paths through the graph. Enables efficient
haplotype-aware operations.

cards.front:
GBZ files use extension [...] and can be built with
vg gbwt or vg autoindex.
cards.back:
GBZ files use extension **.gbz** and can be built with
vg gbwt or vg autoindex.

cards.front:
GBZ files use extension .gbz and can be built with
[...] or vg autoindex.
cards.back:
GBZ files use extension .gbz and can be built with
**vg gbwt** or vg autoindex.

cards.front:
GBZ files use extension .gbz and can be built with
vg gbwt or [...].
cards.back:
GBZ files use extension .gbz and can be built with
vg gbwt or **vg autoindex**.

cards.front: What graph formats can vg read?
cards.back:
- `.vg` - Original protobuf format (mutable, large)
- `.xg` - XG index (immutable, fast random access)
- `.gbz` - GBZ format (immutable, haplotype-aware)
- `.gfa` - GFA text format (interchange)
- `.pg` - PackedGraph (mutable, compact)

cards.front: Why prefer GBZ over XG for Giraffe?
cards.back:
GBZ includes GBWT haplotypes, enabling:
- Haplotype-consistent alignment
- Better scoring with haplotype information
- Smaller file size with path compression

cards.front: What is a GBWTGraph?
cards.back:
A HandleGraph implementation backed by GBWT.
Nodes and edges are derived from the haplotype paths.
Memory-efficient for graphs with many haplotypes.

cards.front: What does the distance index store?
cards.back:
A hierarchical snarl decomposition of the graph that enables
fast computation of shortest distances between any two positions.

cards.front:
Distance index is built with [...]
and stored in .dist files.
cards.back:
Distance index is built with **vg index -j**
and stored in .dist files.

cards.front:
Distance index is built with vg index -j
and stored in [...] files.
cards.back:
Distance index is built with vg index -j
and stored in **.dist** files.

cards.front: What is a snarl?
cards.back:
A subgraph with exactly two boundary nodes (start and end) where
all paths entering through start must exit through end, and vice versa.
Represents a "bubble" or variant site in the graph.

cards.front: What is a chain in the snarl tree?
cards.back:
A sequence of snarls connected end-to-end, where the end node
of one snarl is the start node of the next. Chains alternate
with snarls in the hierarchy.

cards.front: What is the snarl tree hierarchy (top to bottom)?
cards.back:
1. Root (contains entire graph)
2. Chains (sequences of connected snarls)
3. Snarls (bubble structures)
4. Nodes (leaf level)

Chains contain snarls, snarls contain chains or nodes.

cards.front: Why does Giraffe need the distance index?
cards.back:
For clustering seeds. After finding minimizer hits, Giraffe
groups nearby seeds using distance queries to identify
candidate alignment regions.

cards.front:
The distance index is [...] by default.
In HPC environments, make it read-only to avoid conflicts.
cards.back:
The distance index is **memory-mapped** by default.
In HPC environments, make it read-only to avoid conflicts.

cards.front:
The distance index is memory-mapped by default.
In HPC environments, make it [...] to avoid conflicts.
cards.back:
The distance index is memory-mapped by default.
In HPC environments, make it **read-only** to avoid conflicts.

cards.front: What are zipcodes in the context of distance index?
cards.back:
Compressed distance annotations stored with minimizer positions.
Enable faster distance lookups by caching hierarchical snarl
information at each position.

cards.front: What are the main stages of the Giraffe pipeline?
cards.back:
1. **Seeding** - Find minimizer hits in the graph
2. **Clustering** - Group nearby seeds by distance
3. **Chain finding** - Order seeds into collinear chains
4. **Alignment** - Extend chains to full alignments
5. **Scoring** - Select best alignment(s)

cards.front: What is seeding in Giraffe?
cards.back:
Finding minimizer matches between the read and the graph.
Minimizers are sampled k-mers that represent the read.
Each hit gives a (read_pos, graph_pos) pair.

cards.front: What is a minimizer?
cards.back:
The lexicographically smallest k-mer in a window of w k-mers.
Provides a sparse but representative sample of k-mers.
Reduces index size while maintaining sensitivity.

cards.front: How does Giraffe cluster seeds?
cards.back:
Uses the distance index to compute pairwise distances
between seed positions. Seeds within a distance threshold
are grouped into the same cluster.

cards.front: What is chaining in Giraffe?
cards.back:
Finding the best ordered subset of seeds in a cluster
that could come from a single alignment. Uses dynamic
programming on seed positions.

cards.front:
Giraffe requires: a [...] graph, a distance index,
a minimizer index, and a zipcodes file.
cards.back:
Giraffe requires: a **GBZ** graph, a distance index,
a minimizer index, and a zipcodes file.

cards.front:
Giraffe requires: a GBZ graph, a [...] index,
a minimizer index, and a zipcodes file.
cards.back:
Giraffe requires: a GBZ graph, a **distance** index,
a minimizer index, and a zipcodes file.

cards.front:
Giraffe requires: a GBZ graph, a distance index,
a [...] index, and a zipcodes file.
cards.back:
Giraffe requires: a GBZ graph, a distance index,
a **minimizer** index, and a zipcodes file.

cards.front:
Giraffe requires: a GBZ graph, a distance index,
a minimizer index, and a [...] file.
cards.back:
Giraffe requires: a GBZ graph, a distance index,
a minimizer index, and a **zipcodes** file.

cards.front: What aligner does Giraffe use for extension?
cards.back:
WFA (Wavefront Alignment) via the WFA2-lib.
A fast exact algorithm for edit distance alignment.
Extends chains to full read alignments.

cards.front: Short reads vs long reads in Giraffe - key difference?
cards.back:
**Short reads**: Single chain usually sufficient
**Long reads**: May need multiple chains stitched together,
uses different chaining parameters, produces GAF output.

cards.front: What is the XG index?
cards.back:
XG is a space-efficient immutable graph. It is typically used in **mappers** and other applications that do not modify the graph. Multiple graphs can be combined into a single XG index with `vg index -x`. By default, the variants (alt paths) created with `vg construct -a` are not stored as paths in the XG index. They can be included with option `-L`. A single graph can be converted into XG format with `vg convert -x`.

Extension: `.xg`

cards.front: What is the GBWTGraph / GBZ index?
cards.back:
GBWTGraph is an immutable graph induced by the paths stored in an GBWT index. It uses the GBWT for graph topology and stores the sequences in the graph itself. Nodes and edges of the original graph not used on any GBWT path are not included in the GBWTGraph. Because any changes to the GBWT index make the GBWTGraph invalid, **standalone GBWTGraph files are no longer supported**.

Extension: `.gbz`
Build command: `vg gbwt -g`

cards.front: How do you build a GBWTGraph / GBZ index?
cards.back: `vg gbwt -g`

cards.front: What is the GCSA index?
cards.back:
GCSA (sometimes called GCSA2) is an FM-index of a pruned de Bruijn graph that approximates the original graph. Queries up to a certain length (typically 256 bp) map perfectly to the original graph (or its subgraph if the graph was complex and had to be pruned). Longer queries may yield false positives. In most applications, **GCSA also needs the LCP array** for additional functionality. A GCSA index can be built with `vg index -g`. The inputs are typically pruned single-chromosome graphs.

Extension: `.gcsa`
Build command: `vg index -g`

cards.front: How do you build a GCSA index?
cards.back: `vg index -g`

cards.front: What is the GBWT index?
cards.back:
The GBWT is an FM-index that stores similar paths space-efficiently. In most applications, it is used for storing (real or artificial) **haplotypes**. A GBWT index may also contain metadata with structured (sample, contig, haplotype, fragment) names for each path. Paths with sample name `_gbwt_ref` are often interpreted as generic paths.

Extension: `.gbwt`

cards.front: What is the Distance index index?
cards.back:
A distance index stores a hierarchical snarl decomposition of the graph and uses it for computing shortest distances between positions in the graph. The index is built with `vg index -j`.

Extension: `.dist`
Build command: `vg index -j`

cards.front: How do you build a Distance index index?
cards.back: `vg index -j`

cards.front: What is the Zipcodes file index?
cards.back:
A zipcodes file stores "zipcode" information for seed kmers in the graph, when that information is too long to embed directly in the minimizer index (see below). The zipcodes file is built with `vg minimizer` at the same time as the minimizer index, by using the `-z`/`--zipcode-name` option.

Extension: `.zipcodes`
Build command: `vg minimizer`

cards.front: How do you build a Zipcodes file index?
cards.back: `vg minimizer`

cards.front: What is the Minimizer index index?
cards.back:
A minimizer index stores a subset of kmers from the haplotypes and the corresponding graph positions in a hash table. The positions must be annotated with distance information for faster distance index queries. Minimizer indexes are built with `vg minimizer`. The construction requires a GBZ graph.

Extension: `.withzip.min`
Build command: `vg minimizer`

cards.front: How do you build a Minimizer index index?
cards.back: `vg minimizer`

cards.front: What is the `vg map` and `vg mpmap` index?
cards.back: The `vg map` and `vg mpmap` workflows require a graph (usually XG index) and a GCSA index with the LCP array. They may also uses a GBWT index with haplotypes for (potentially) more accurate alignment scores.

cards.front: What is VG Protobuf?
cards.back:
The original vg graph format
Extension: `.vg`
Status: Conditionally useful
Notes: Can also be used to store paths without the nodes and edges they belong to. Default output format of `vg construct` in vg v1.40.0, since it can be generated incrementally. Can be concatenated with `cat`. Usually block-GZIP compressed, but some old files aren't. Consists of count-prefixed groups of length-prefixed Protobuf messages, where a string type tag takes the place of the first message in each group.

cards.back: `.vg`

cards.front: What is GBZ?
cards.back:
"GBZ" graph, a compressed format storing a graph as traversed by sample haplotypes
Extension: `.gbz`
Status: Recommended
Notes: Stores not only the graph but also large numbers of haplotypes, so you don't need an additional GBWT file. Internally, stores a GBWT and a GBWTGraph. Can't store edges that are not followed.

cards.back: `.gbz`

cards.front: What is a snarl?
cards.back: A topological motif where two or more alternative paths exist between two boundary nodes. A generalization of a 'bubble'. Represents variable sequence flanked by conserved sequence.

cards.front: What are the two properties that define a snarl?
cards.back:
1. Separable: splitting boundary nodes disconnects the snarl from the rest of the graph
2. Minimal: no internal node is separable with the boundary nodes

cards.front: What is a chain in the snarl decomposition?
cards.back: A sequence of consecutive snarls with shared boundary nodes between them. For example, if snarl 1-4 and snarl 4-6 share node 4, they form chain 1-6.

cards.front: What are the boundary nodes of a snarl?
cards.back: The two nodes (x and y) that delimit a snarl's subgraph. They are the entry and exit points of the variable region.

cards.front: How is an SNP represented in a variation graph?
cards.back: Two allele nodes (e.g., nodes 2 and 3) connected between two flanking conserved nodes (e.g., 1 and 4). Forms a simple snarl.

cards.front: How is an indel represented in a variation graph?
cards.back:
Insertion: a node for inserted sequence between boundary nodes.
Deletion: an edge bypassing the deleted sequence node.

cards.front: What is the snarl tree hierarchy (top to bottom)?
cards.back:
1. Root (contains entire graph)
2. Chains (sequences of connected snarls)
3. Snarls (bubble structures)
4. Nodes (leaf level)

Chains and snarls alternate in the hierarchy.

cards.front: How is a duplication represented in a variation graph?
cards.back: A node with an edge from its end back to its start (self-loop). A path can traverse the node multiple times.

cards.front: How is an inversion represented in a variation graph?
cards.back: A node that can be traversed in either direction. Its start and end are each connected to both the previous and next nodes.

cards.front: What indexes does Giraffe require?
cards.back:
1. GBZ graph (contains GBWT + GBWTGraph)
2. Distance index (.dist)
3. Minimizer index (.withzip.min)
4. Zipcodes file (.zipcodes)

cards.front: Why should the distance index be read-only in HPC environments?
cards.back: As of vg 1.48.0, the distance index is memory-mapped in read+write mode by default. Multiple nodes accessing the same file causes conflicts. Make it read-only or use local copies.

cards.front: What graph structures does Giraffe prefer?
cards.back: Graphs that avoid complex structures at every level: low-degree nodes, no collapsed repetitive regions, no long-distance edges. Minimize sequence duplication.

cards.front: How do you specify index files explicitly in Giraffe?
cards.back:
-Z / --gbz-name: GBZ graph
-d / --dist-name: distance index
-m / --minimizer-name: minimizer index
-z / --zipcode-name: zipcodes file

cards.front: What happens if you don't provide zipcode annotations to Giraffe?
cards.back: Mapping speed will be slow. Always build the minimizer index with -d (distance index) and -z (zipcode output) options.

cards.front: Difference between short-read and long-read Giraffe indexes?
cards.back:
Different k values for minimizers.
Short read: .shortread.zipcodes, .shortread.withzip.min
Long read: .longread.zipcodes, .longread.withzip.min

cards.front: What is the easiest way to build all Giraffe indexes?
cards.back: `vg autoindex` - automatically builds GBZ, distance index, minimizer index, and zipcodes from input FASTA + VCF.

cards.front: What is a HandleGraph?
cards.back:
The base interface for all graph implementations in vg.
Provides read-only access to nodes and edges via opaque "handles".

cards.front: What is a "handle" in HandleGraph?
cards.back:
An opaque reference to a node orientation (forward or reverse).
Encodes both node ID and strand in a single 64-bit value.

cards.front: Method: get the sequence of a node from its handle?
cards.back:
```cpp
std::string get_sequence(const handle_t& handle) const
```
Returns the sequence in the orientation of the handle.

cards.front: Method: iterate over all edges from a handle?
cards.back:
```cpp
bool follow_edges(const handle_t& handle, bool go_left,
                  const std::function<bool(const handle_t&)>& iteratee) const
```
Calls iteratee for each neighbor. go_left=true for incoming edges.

The handle to the same node but in the opposite orientation.
